\chapter{Writing --- Four Lines About You}
\label{ch:escribir-ficha-personal}
\hlchaptermodality{338}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can fill a personal-information form with my name, age, origin and address, using only frames I already hold.}

Complete ES-W01-ficha-personal: write four frames about yourself in the order a form asks for them, and stop when the four facts are down.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Four lines about you}

\label{lesson:ES-W01-ficha-personal}



\begin{quote}
Last time you chose two things and put them in an order. Nothing new went on the page, and it was still your own line.

Now four of them, and the same rule holds: no word you have not already been given.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — controlled composition}
A clinic asks the person at the desk to write four facts about themselves. Here is your whole supply:

\begin{quote}
\emph{me llamo} · \emph{tengo … años} · \emph{soy de …} · \emph{vivo en …} · \emph{gracias}
\end{quote}

Write four lines. Your name, your age, where you are from, where you live — then close with the courtesy word.

Each line is a frame with one blank you fill from your own life:

\begin{quote}
\emph{Me llamo} \_\_\_\_\_\_. \emph{Tengo} \_\_\_\_\_\_ \emph{años.} \emph{Soy de} \_\_\_\_\_\_. \emph{Vivo en} \_\_\_\_\_\_.
\end{quote}

Then \emph{gracias} on its own line.

Two things are being asked of you, and only one of them is Spanish. The Spanish is the frames, and you have held every one of them for a long time. The other thing is deciding which frame answers which question, and stopping when the four facts are on the page. Writing what was asked and nothing more is a skill of its own.

Now compare. \emph{Soy de} names the place you came from; \emph{vivo en} names the place you are now. If both of your blanks hold the same word, that is a true answer, not a mistake — plenty of people never moved.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} your four lines aloud, and hear that every word was already yours
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How many words on your page were new? (\textbf{None.})

And which verb carries your age? (\emph{\textbf{Tener}} — you \emph{have} the years.) Next: the same four lines, with a clock running.
\end{tcolorbox}
